_comment: Curated symptom -> cause -> fix knowledge for reactviro_diagnose_error. Each trap's `symptoms` are matched case-insensitively as substrings against the caller's error text — keep them short and distinctive (an exact fragment of a real message), not full sentences. Edit here to add a trap without touching code. Sourced from viro/CLAUDE.md's 'Known traps' section and bugs actually caught by reactviro_render_scene during development — add to this file whenever a new one is found the same way.

traps.title: Raw event prop leaks through a spread and crashes iOS at mount, with no JS logs
traps.explanation: A component built its native props via `Object.assign({}, this.props)` (or an equivalent spread) without scrubbing out React-only event props first. A raw JS `onClick` (or similar `onX`) function leaked into the native props bridge, and the native side tried to call a native setter (`setOnClick:`) that doesn't exist for a JS function value.
traps.fix: Before assigning props to the native bridge, explicitly set `nativeProps.onClick = undefined` (and any other event handler prop) so only the bridge's own synthetic handler is sent across. `unrecognized selector setOnX:` on any VRT-prefixed native class is this pattern — it will not show up in JS console logs, only in the native crash log (Sentry/Crashlytics), so a log-less scene-open crash on a real device is the first sign.

traps.title: VROGeospatial.h enum values differ between iOS and Android builds of the same native header
traps.explanation: virocore has two copies of VROGeospatial.h (ios/ViroKit/VROGeospatial.h using `Enabled`, ViroRenderer/VROGeospatial.h using `Tracking` for the same state) sharing one include guard. Xcode's real "Copy Headers" build phase flattens both into one directory with ios/ViroKit's copy winning; Android's CMake build never sees that copy at all, so it consistently gets the other one. A naive standalone compile check that just adds both directories to the include path (instead of replicating Xcode's flatten-with-override) produces a false-positive missing-member error.
traps.fix: Any change to this enum must be applied to BOTH header copies, appended at the end — never inserted in the middle, since Android's JNI bridge (ARScene.java) maps the enum to Java by raw ordinal position, not by name. To reproduce Xcode's real resolution outside Xcode, build a staging include directory that copies ViroRenderer/*.h first, then ios/ViroKit/*.h on top, before compiling standalone.

traps.title: Viro3DScene / ViroVRScene don't exist — the scene wrapper is generic ViroScene
symptoms: expected a string (for built-in components) or a class/function
traps.explanation: Only ViroARScene is a real, navigator-specific scene component. 3D and VR both use the generic ViroScene for scene content — there is no Viro3DScene or ViroVRScene in @reactvision/react-viro. Code that assumes a `Viro${navigatorType}Scene` naming convention (matching the real `Viro${navigatorType}SceneNavigator`) will reference a component that doesn't exist, and React reports it as an invalid element type.
traps.fix: Use `<ViroARScene>` only when navigating with ViroARSceneNavigator; use the generic `<ViroScene>` for both Viro3DSceneNavigator and ViroVRSceneNavigator. This exact bug existed in reactviro_generate_scene's own template until it was caught by rendering the generated code through reactviro_render_scene — see src/tools/scene.ts's sceneComponentName().

traps.title: Passing a component (a function) straight into a useState setter gets called as the updater, not stored
symptoms: Did you accidentally export a JSX literal instead of a component
traps.explanation: React's `useState` setter treats a bare function argument as an updater callback (`setState(prev => next)`), not as the literal new value. Code that dynamically resolves a component and does `setSomeComponent(TheComponent)` (e.g. loading a scene component from a compiled module) actually gets `TheComponent` CALLED once with the previous state as its argument, and the component's RETURN VALUE (an already-instantiated element) ends up stored as state instead of the component itself. The resulting React error ("expected ... but got: <View />" or similar) is confusing because it names whatever the top-level JSX in that returned element happens to be, not the real cause.
traps.fix: Wrap it: `setSomeComponent(() => TheComponent)`. Any code path that stores a dynamically-loaded/compiled component in useState should use the same pattern.

traps.title: A .web.tsx component that calls require() at module scope breaks under Vite (or any non-Metro bundler)
traps.explanation: Some .web.tsx files (e.g. ViroSpinner.web.tsx, for its built-in PNGs) carry over Metro's `require('./Resources/x.png')` convention. Metro provides a global `require`; Vite (and most other bundlers) do not — the file throws the moment it's imported, even if the component is never actually rendered, because ES module bodies execute fully on import.
traps.fix: Replace the module-scope `require(...)` with a bundler-agnostic asset import (e.g. Vite's `?url` import) behind a platform check, or lazy-load the asset only when the component actually mounts. Until fixed at the source, any web harness/tool that imports such a component wholesale (rather than only when used) must exclude it and degrade gracefully instead of crashing every render that merely imports the module — see viro/web-harness/viroWebComponents.ts's handling of ViroSpinner.
